Treatment details

    Surface absorption assumptions

    Energy absorbed per hit at the selected band. These are editable scenario values, not measured materials. They stay fixed when you change band.

    Blue and rose show opposite pressure phases; dark bands are nodes. This is a horizontal slice at listener height in an ideal rigid, empty room. Amplitude is normalized, not SPL. Absorption panels do not change this ideal mode model.

    Corner and boundary pressure maxima identify places to investigate bass treatment. Thickness, tuning and decay need a measured low-frequency response; no bass-trap performance is predicted here.

    Listener & playback

    Speaker data & model limits

    Propagation uses geometric distance / sound speed, specular reflections and energy loss at boundaries. Smooth beam shapes assume nominal angles correspond to −6 dB; actual frequency-dependent polar files are unavailable. Directional models are held fixed across bands. Up to four direct paths and three first-order reflections are shown. Rings and trails indicate direction; they are not pressure wavefronts. Equal source strength; cabinet diffraction, scattering, air absorption, DSP and phase interference are not simulated. Sabine assumes a diffuse field and estimates decay independently of the drawn rays. Cabinet shapes remain stand-ins; GC118 height is assumed.

    Bass uses exact rectangular-room eigenmode shapes with ideal rigid boundaries. Source coupling assumes equal, in-phase sources within their published response ranges; it does not model a crossover or predict driven SPL. System counts remain concept configurations, not validated room recommendations.

    Image-source and ray methods ↗
    Rectangular-room modes ↗

    Absorption or sound isolation?

    Green panels address reflections inside the room. They are not a soundproofing specification. Sound escaping outside depends on wall, ceiling, floor and door assemblies, gaps and flanking paths. This app does not predict transmission loss or neighbour levels. Those construction details and site measurements are needed before recommending isolation work.

    The room is yours.

    Move the slider to grow the space. Click or tap a speaker in the room, or select it on the left, to inspect it up close.

    Drag to look around.

    Click the room, then hold WASD or the arrow keys to walk. On touchscreens, hold the movement arrows and drag the scene to look around. Reset view returns you to the starting position. Press Escape to close this panel or leave a product view.

    About this preview

    Product names come from Tub’s catalogue. The models are visual stand-ins. Pairings and room-size thresholds are illustrative, not acoustic predictions.
